tldr: Kickoff meeting for a new remote control project; Sarah, the project manager, outlined the agenda and the three design phases: functional, conceptual and detailed.
The team did a whiteboard warm-up drawing favourite animals (tiger, dog, crocodile, eagle) and listing their traits.
Finance targets: 25 euro selling price (about 17 pounds), 12.50 euro production cost, 50 million euro profit aim. The team noted market rivals sell at about 20 pounds.

Design ideas floated: few main buttons with a menu for other functions, an LCD with phone-style menus, a large-print button, a flip-top, and lightweight plastic. Cost and usability for older users were flagged as concerns.
Everyone goes off to do individual work and reconvenes after about half an hour.

actions.text: Put the meeting notes and the presentation in the shared folders so the team can refer back to them.
Do individual design work, then reconvene for the next meeting.

questions: How should the design serve older users, who may struggle with menus and programming?
Can an LCD screen or a flip-top fit within the 12.50 euro production cost?
Does plastic make the product cheaper, and does it fit the company's fashion-in-electronics image?
Should the price undercut the roughly 20 pound market price, or would that make the product look cheap?
Is the 50 million euro profit aim meant for the first year? Sarah presumed so but was not sure.
